scope: Native SDL3.2.18 keyboard/controller startup through the original cdecl guest ABI.
behavior: Initialize real native JOYSTICK, GAMEPAD and HAPTIC subsystems under the Apple application main thread. Preserve native success, failure, reference counts and dependency shutdown.
Copy the actual native bool keyboard state into a stable checked borrowed guest array. Refresh on queries; copy the native scancode count to the optional guest output.

Copy native gamepad IDs and their zero terminator into caller-owned guest allocator storage. Native enumeration memory is immediately SDL_free'd; ordinary guest SDL_free releases the returned array. Allocation failure returns zero, clears the output count and preserves SDL OutOfMemory.

Use process-qualified, nonreused typed tokens for native gamepads. Repeated opens preserve native reference counts and handle identity; final close releases borrowed name copies. Names are refreshed on queries while earlier snapshots remain valid through close. Final subsystem shutdown and SDL_Quit clear the registry.

Preserve CPU state, cdecl arguments and Win32 LastError. Reject stale or wrong-type handles, modified borrowed snapshots, inaccessible guest outputs and incompatible native call signatures. Native pointers never become guest pointers.
limits: The guest event pump and SDL event-union conversion are not implemented. The future pump must refresh the borrowed keyboard array after native event processing and before invoking guest handlers.
Axis/button polling, rumble and other gamepad APIs remain separate reached-consumer work. Native virtual-controller tests establish bridge behavior, not physical controls or gameplay acceptance.
Original rendering, full-engine UIKit hosting, HD gameplay and authenticated multiplayer remain unverified.
